verdict.rationale: Lindy documents a credentials store that it uses when running shell commands and code. Saved keys are private to the owner until explicitly shared with the workspace, so central storage and team sharing are covered. Access control is only binary (just me vs. everyone in the workspace), with no documented per-user, per-group, or per-credential permissions. missing for 10: granular control over who can use which credential (role/user/group scoping), admin governance over shared credentials, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can store connection credentials centrally, share them with my team, and control who can use which credential

citations.quote: Credentials are what Lindy reaches for when it runs shell commands and code.
Save a key and only you can use it, until you choose to share it with everyone in the workspace.
